raw_response:
I’m 65 now, and I’ve farmed this land long enough to know that steady management is better than chasing fancy ideas. On 8 mu, with only two people in the household and some off-farm work, I can’t afford a plan that needs too much labor or too much cash all at once. So this year I’ll keep the wheat-maize rotation on all 8 mu. Wheat is still the backbone here, and maize follows right after harvest, so I won’t leave land idle. Because irrigation from the well costs money, I’ll use water at the key stages instead of watering too often. I have enough experience to adjust inputs a bit by crop stage, but I still stay close to what has worked on my fields before. For wheat, I want a solid stand before winter, so I’ll use a good local improved variety, put on base fertilizer at sowing, then topdress once at jointing. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple and plant quickly with a hybrid seed that emerges fast and yields steadily. I’d rather spend a bit more on reliable seed and adequate nitrogen than risk weak growth, but I won’t push fertilizer too high because 8 mu is small and every yuan still matters.
